Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

Sixteen months after BCG he developed bilateral knee pain, worse on the left, without systemic symptoms. Examination showed mild warmth and effusions; vital signs were stable. Inflammatory markers were modestly raised (ESR 32 mm/h, CRP 1.6 mg/L, procalcitonin 0.1 ng/mL) with normal blood count and liver tests. Imaging did not show loosening or overt infection. Right‑knee aspirate Gram stain and routine cultures were negative; synovial cell count and chemistry are unavailable. Acid‑fast stain was negative, but delayed mycobacterial culture grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Strain identification and outcome data are pending.

Hypotheses: the isolate may represent BCG‑derived Mycobacterium bovis, a reactivated Mycobacterium tuberculosis, or a laboratory contaminant. The long latency after BCG and the bilateral involvement raise the possibility of haematogenous seeding of both prostheses.

Proposed actions before any management decision: (1) request definitive speciation (e.g., PCR, whole‑genome sequencing) and drug‑susceptibility testing of the isolate; (2) obtain left‑knee aspiration for cell count, chemistry, acid‑fast stain, culture and mycobacterial PCR; (3) refer to an infectious‑diseases physician and a revision arthroplasty surgeon for joint assessment; (4) evaluate for disseminated disease (chest imaging, HIV test, interferon‑gamma release assay).
